blocks.text:
Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. # Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level
# ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original
# monolith semantics — every gate, full thresholds — on a nightly schedule.
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve

            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)

          try:

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original
# monolith semantics — every gate, full thresholds — on a nightly schedule.
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a

name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:

jobs:
  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # without it the analyzer fails with asset_does_not_exist (a fresh
      # clone hits the same warning locally).
      - name: Create placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored (real keys stay local); the
      # repo-wide analyze fails on the unresolved import without it. The
      # tracked placeholder makes it compile (Firebase init is skipped for
      # YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      - name: dart analyze
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart test --coverage (excluding integration)
        run: dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Coverage ratchet (lib/ >= 80%)
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        run: |
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.9.5"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

  # PTY/terminal integration suites (issue #177 follow-up): mock-endpoint
  # tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests self-skip
  # gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the blanket
  # "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone. Coverage over
  # lib/src/cli/** feeds the only-up ratchet (coverage-gardener.yml bumps
  # the baseline weekly) — terminal-test coverage can never silently drop.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PTY runner picker: prefer the self-hosted fa-m5 minis (dedicated hardware,
  # warm caches, no VM boot, no port contention — the hosted pty-integration
  # leg loses 20-40 min to queue+load flake), fall back to the hosted labels

    name: Pick PTY runners (fa-m5 or hosted fallback)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      actions: read
    outputs:
      pty_integration: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_integration }}
      pty_visual: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_visual }}

- name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # Main remains backstopped by nightly.yml.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PTY runner picker: prefer the self-hosted fa-m5 minis (dedicated hardware,
  # warm caches, no VM boot, no port contention — the hosted pty-integration
  # leg loses 20-40 min to queue+load flake), fall back to the hosted labels

  # the choice happens HERE by counting in-progress jobs already parked on

            busy=$((busy + n))
          done
          free=$((M5_POOL - busy))
          if [ "$free" -ge 1 ]; then
            echo "pool: $free free of $M5_POOL fa-m5 -> self-hosted"
            echo 'pty_integration=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

            echo 'pty_integration=["ubuntu-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["macos-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration + cli coverage (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read

      # Trust model (review 2026-09-23): this is the first pull_request-time
      # leg in ci.yml that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds
      # secrets from forks, so external contributions never see them — but
      # every SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process

      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # SAME secret shape as nightly.yml's pty-integration leg and the
      # coverage-gardener that bumps the baseline: the live-provider legs
      # (unlocked by these keys) load extra lib/src/cli surface into the
      # measurement, so a no-key run measures a DIFFERENT — higher —
      # number and would pass while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      # coverage-gardener that bumps the baseline: the live-provider legs

      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext)

          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage
      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration

        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/

1. `runner-pick` job: uses `github.token` with `actions: read` — fine.
2. The probe loop: iterates over ALL in-progress runs in the repo (up to 100 per page), and for each run fetches jobs. This is N+1 API calls — could be slow and hit rate limits. Also `per_page=100` only gets the first page — runs beyond 100 are not counted. Race conditions: counting in-progress jobs is inherently racy.
3. `runner_name` field: is `runner_name` available in the jobs API for jobs queued/in_progress? Actually `runner_name` is available in the jobs API response (it's in the job object). For queued jobs, runner_name is null. For in-progress jobs on self-hosted, runner_name should be populated. OK.
4. Busy counting logic: `free = M5_POOL - busy`; if free >= 2, use self-hosted for BOTH jobs (pty_integration AND pty_visual). But wait — M5_POOL = 3 and both jobs together need 2 runners... but each job might run on the same runner sequentially or on different runners. Also, pty_visual on self-hosted requires macOS? The labels "self-hosted" and "macos-m5" — pty_visual was macos-latest before, meaning the visual leg needs macOS. If fa-m5 minis are macOS machines... need to check. The label `macos-m5` suggests macOS M5 minis. Hmm, "fa-m5" = Apple M5 Mac mini? Presumably.

Big issue: **outputs with arrays via fromJSON** — `runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}` — GITHUB_OUTPUT multi-line strings: `echo 'pty_integration=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` — this writes a single-line string containing JSON. fromJSON parses it into an array. That's the standard pattern. OK.
6. **Security concern with self-hosted runners**: Self-hosted runners executing `pull_request` events from forks are dangerous (no sandbox isolation). But this is nightly.yml — which presumably triggers on `schedule` and maybe `workflow_dispatch`, not pull_request. Let me check the nightly.yml triggers. If nightly only runs on schedule/dispatch in the base repo, the risk is lower, though secrets are still exposed to the self-hosted runner. Self-hosted runners running workflow code with access to secrets — the runner itself is trusted infra presumably. But a known GitHub security caveat: secrets on self-hosted runners... The repo's own token and secrets (OLLAMA_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY?) are exposed to jobs on self-hosted runners. That's presumably intended.

But wait — there's a subtle issue: setting `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE` via GITHUB_ENV at runtime does NOT affect where setup-dart installs the SDK? Actually, `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses DART_HOME... Hmm. setup-dart downloads the SDK into the tool cache (`RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/dart/...`)? Changing RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE via GITHUB_ENV in a previous step does affect subsequent steps' env, and setup-dart reads RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE at execution time to decide where to put the SDK. Actually setup-dart's Node script reads `process.env['RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE']`, which would be set by GITHUB_ENV by then. So it should work. The motivation: self-hosted runners share a tool cache; pointing it into the runner workspace avoids permission/contention issues. Hmm, but is it per-workspace? `runner.workspace` is like `/home/runner/work/<repo>/<repo>`... on self-hosted with persistent workspaces, multiple concurrent jobs on the SAME runner share the workspace path? No — workspace is per-job? Actually `runner.workspace` = the default working directory root, e.g., `/home/runner/work/<repo-name>/<repo-name>`. On the same runner, concurrent jobs can't run anyway (one job at a time per runner), unless the mini pool has multiple runner processes per machine. If two runner processes are registered on the same machine (e.g., 3 minis with maybe 1 runner each = pool of 3), the workspaces are distinct per runner registration. OK.

But a real issue: pty_integration and pty_visual may BOTH be routed to self-hosted, and if pool is 3 minis and 2 jobs need 2 runners, fine. But what about pty_visual needing macOS-specific stuff? If fa-m5 are mac minis with label macos-m5 + self-hosted, fine.

Two legs launched: both runner-pick picks happen before the legs start (runner-pick runs first), so at probe time zero fa-m5 jobs are in progress from THIS run — the count `busy` only reflects OTHER runs. free >= 2 → both legs go self-hosted. Actually more precisely: `busy` counts jobs with status "in_progress" on runners named fa-m5*. If a job is "queued" pending on a fa-m5 runner (because a minis is busy), it's not counted, so free is overestimated. Two concurrent nightly runs → both pick self-hosted → oversubscription → one leg queues behind the other for potentially hours. The whole motivation is flake under load/queueing. # Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level
# ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original
# monolith semantics — every gate, full thresholds — on a nightly schedule.
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # without it the analyzer fails with asset_does_not_exist (a fresh
      # clone hits the same warning locally).
      - name: Create placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored (real keys stay local); the
      # repo-wide analyze fails on the unresolved import without it. The
      # tracked placeholder makes it compile (Firebase init is skipped for
      # YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      - name: dart analyze
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart test --coverage (excluding integration)
        run: dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Coverage ratchet (lib/ >= 80%)
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        run: |
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.9.5"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

  # PTY/terminal integration suites (issue #177 follow-up): mock-endpoint
  # tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests self-skip
  # gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the blanket
  # "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone. Coverage over
  # lib/src/cli/** feeds the only-up ratchet (coverage-gardener.yml bumps
  # the baseline weekly) — terminal-test coverage can never silently drop.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PTY runner picker: prefer the self-hosted fa-m5 minis (dedicated hardware,
  # warm caches, no VM boot, no port contention — the hosted pty-integration
  # leg loses 20-40 min to queue+load flake), fall back to the hosted labels
  # when the pool is busy. GitHub has no OR in runs-on (an array is AND), so
  # the choice happens HERE by counting in-progress jobs already parked on
  # fa-m5 runners (jobs API, actions:read — no admin token needed).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  runner-pick:
    name: Pick PTY runners (fa-m5 or hosted fallback)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      actions: read
    outputs:
      pty_integration: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_integration }}
      pty_visual: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_visual }}
    steps:
      - name: Probe fa-m5 pool and pick
        id: pick
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          M5_POOL: '3'
        run: |
          busy=0
          for rid in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?status=in_progress&per_page=100" --jq '.workflow_runs[].id'); do
            n=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$rid/jobs" --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" and ((.runner_name // "") | startswith("fa-m5")))] | length' || echo 0)
            busy=$((busy + n))
          done
          free=$((M5_POOL - busy))
          if [ "$free" -ge 2 ]; then
            echo "pool: $free free of $M5_POOL fa-m5 -> self-hosted"
            echo 'pty_integration=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "pool: $free free of $M5_POOL fa-m5 -> hosted fallback"
            echo 'pty_integration=["ubuntu-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["macos-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

    name: PTY/CLI integration + cli coverage
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: runner-pick
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}

- name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # Main remains backstopped by nightly.yml.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PTY runner picker: prefer the self-hosted fa-m5 minis (dedicated hardware,
  # warm caches, no VM boot, no port contention — the hosted pty-integration
  # leg loses 20-40 min to queue+load flake), fall back to the hosted labels
  # when the pool is busy. GitHub has no OR in runs-on (an array is AND), so
  # the choice happens HERE by counting in-progress jobs already parked on
  # fa-m5 runners (jobs API, actions:read — no admin token needed).

Now I have a clear picture. Key observations comparing nightly.yml's new runner-pick against the existing reference implementation in ci.yml (#860):

**Differences between nightly.yml (this PR) and ci.yml (reference):**

1. **Threshold `free >= 2` vs `free >= 1`**:
   - nightly.yml (this PR): `if [ "$free" -ge 2 ]` → BOTH legs go self-hosted (needs 2 runners simultaneously).
   - ci.yml (reference): `if [ "$free" -ge 1 ]` → both legs go self-hosted if at least 1 free.
   
   Wait, this is interesting — this PR uses `-ge 2` and the reference uses `-ge 1`. Which is right? In nightly, BOTH pty-integration and cli-visual would run concurrently on self-hosted (2 runners needed concurrently, since runner-pick is the only needs, both legs start in parallel). Actually — do they run concurrently? pty-integration and cli-visual both depend only on runner-pick, so yes, they start in parallel. So needing 2 free is arguably MORE correct in nightly than ci.yml's `>= 1`. In ci.yml, with `>= 1`, if only 1 mini is free, one leg grabs it and the other queues on self-hosted... hmm, both jobs request `["self-hosted","macos-m5"]`, so with 1 free runner, one leg starts and the other waits queued (indefinitely?) until a mini frees. GitHub queues self-hosted jobs; they wait until a matching runner is available or the job... queued self-hosted jobs wait forever unless a runner comes online. Actually there's no queue timeout for self-hosted runners by default (jobs can be queued indefinitely? There is a default of 24h? For hosted runners, jobs queued > 24h? Hmm).

   Actually wait — which direction should the reviewer flag? The nightly threshold is arguably better. But there's an inconsistency between the two implementations of the same logic — drift risk. And a subtle behavioral difference: with `-ge 2`, if only 1 mini is free, the nightly falls back to hosted for BOTH legs — but then the 1 free mini sits idle while the hosted legs hit the load flake the PR is trying to avoid. With concurrent jobs = 2, requiring 2 free is the correct conservative approach... but actually it wastes capacity: pty_integration on hosted (flaky) while a mini is idle. Hmm, an alternative would be picking per-leg. Not a blocker; worth a suggestion. Actually wait — is it even true both run simultaneously? runner-pick runs first (3 min max), then both legs start together. So yes, they run concurrently. With pool of 3 and `>= 2`, at least one mini always remains free for... hmm, for what? For ci.yml PR legs (which use `>= 1`)! That's likely deliberate: nightly reserves headroom so PR-time ci.yml legs can still grab a mini. Or so that a concurrent ci.yml run can still get one. Plausibly deliberate. I'll note as a question/suggestion about the divergence from ci.yml's `>= 1` and potential double-booking race.

2. **Race / oversubscription**: counting only `in_progress` jobs, not `queued`. Two nightly-ish runs starting close together (nightly schedule + a manual dispatch, or ci.yml run + nightly run) both probe at roughly the same time before either has jobs in_progress on fa-m5 → both pick self-hosted → legs queue on the minis. Since ci.yml PR legs ALSO run this same probe concurrently (every PR), this race is real: PR-time ci.yml runs and the nightly run will both see free pool and both send jobs to fa-m5. The queued legs then wait on minis with no timeout — nightly.yml's pty-integration and cli-visual have **no timeout-minutes** (I checked the new file: pty-integration has no timeout-minutes; cli-visual has none either), unlike ci.yml's legs (60/45). A queued-on-self-hosted job with no timeout can block the nightly for hours; worse, the auto-issue job has `needs: [full-quality, pty-integration, cli-visual, ...]` with `if: always() && schedule && !cancelled()` — fine, it still files.

   Actually hold on: does GitHub queue self-hosted jobs forever? Jobs queued waiting for a runner will wait until a runner picks them up; there's no default timeout for being queued (the 6-hour job limit applies once running). Hmm, actually if a runner never comes, the job stays queued indefinitely and the run hangs. So the race can genuinely hang the nightly. The mitigating factor: pool busy count includes ci.yml PR legs on fa-m5, so the probe will usually see them. But the probe runs once at runner-pick time; jobs queued after the probe but not yet in_progress are invisible. Flag as IMPORTANT.

3. **N+1 API calls**: The probe loops over up to 100 in-progress runs and makes one `gh api .../runs/$rid/jobs` call per run. In a busy repo (machine-driven PRs — this repo has ai-teammate, machine-merge, etc., so many concurrent runs), that could be dozens of calls; at ~200-500ms each that's 10-30s, OK within timeout-minutes: 3, but with retries/rate limits it could exceed. `gh` auto-retries on 403 rate-limit with backoff (GH_* envs). A cleaner approach: single call to `repos/$REPO/actions/runners` (needs `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners` — that requires... listing self-hosted runners for a repo requires admin:write? Hmm, actually `gh api repos/REPO/actions/runners` — requires `admin:write`? Docs: "List self-hosted runners for a repository" — fine-grained: "Administration" repository permissions (write). GitHub Apps: administration. So indeed not accessible with actions:read — the comment in the workflow explains this ("jobs API, actions:read — no admin token needed"), which justifies the N+1 workaround. The alternative: use the jobs API pagination smarter, or use `gh api /repos/$REPO/actions/runs?status=in_progress` + `--jq` per run is N+1. Alternative single call: `gh run list --json databaseId --limit 100 --status in_progress` then still N+1. Hmm — there's also the check-runs for a ref... Not simpler. So the N+1 is a known tradeoff already established in ci.yml — consistent with reference. I'll mention only briefly (SUGGESTION): `total_count` guard for >100 runs (pagination ignored → undercount → oversubscription).

4. **`per_page=100` no pagination**: in-progress runs beyond the first 100 aren't counted. Machine-generated repos can have >100 in-progress runs. Undercount → self-hosted chosen when pool is actually busy → queueing. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It's shared with the reference ci.yml implementation. I'd rate SUGGESTION (consistent with existing accepted pattern) or fold into the probe-robustness comment.

5. **cli-visual on fa-m5 without the toolcache redirect**: In nightly.yml's cli-visual job, there is NO "Self-hosted toolcache redirect" step, and it routes to `["self-hosted","macos-m5"]` when free. In ci.yml's pty-visual job — let me check... In the reference (ci.yml pty-visual), there's also no redirect step; but ci.yml's pty-visual doesn't run setup-dart... wait it runs flutter-action. Hmm, the redirect in ci.yml was added only to pty-integration ("Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die"). flutter-action (subosito) doesn't use RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE; it downloads to its own cache dir (~/flutter or RUNNER_TEMP?). Hmm wait — subosito/flutter-action downloads the Flutter SDK to `$RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/flutter` by default? No — it defaults to `${{ github.workspace }}/-runners/...`? Let me recall: subosito/flutter-action has a `flutter-version` and downloads into a local dir inside the workspace (`.flutter/`?) Actually I believe subosito/flutter-action extracts into `$RUNNER_TEMP` or a directory near the workspace ("CACHE-FLUTTER" default path is `${{ runner.tool_cache }}/flutter`?). Hmm. In subosito/flutter-action README: "The flutter SDK is downloaded to the $RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/flutter directory" — hmm no, I recall it downloads to a path like `<workspace>/flutter` unless... Let me not over-assert. The important comparability point: ci.yml's pty-visual leg runs the same flutter-action on fa-m5 with NO redirect, and presumably it worked (it's merged and running — the nightly comment says ci.yml legs already run this). So nightly cli-visual matching that is consistent. Not a finding, or a minor note.

   But — wait, in nightly.yml cli-visual, there IS `subosito/flutter-action` with `cache: true`. On self-hosted persistent runners, cache: t…

blocks.text:
# Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level
# ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original
# monolith semantics — every gate, full thresholds — on a nightly schedule.
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # without it the analyzer fails with asset_does_not_exist (a fresh
      # clone hits the same warning locally).
      - name: Create placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored (real keys stay local); the
      # repo-wide analyze fails on the unresolved import without it. The
      # tracked placeholder makes it compile (Firebase init is skipped for
      # YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      - name: dart analyze
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart test --coverage (excluding integration)
        run: dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Coverage ratchet (lib/ >= 80%)
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        run: |
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.9.5"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')

- name: dart test under hostile ambient env
        run: dart test --exclude-tags integration

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Nightly parity (2026-09-23): the two legs that stayed nightly-only went
  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage
  # ratchet (12.07% < 12.17%) and the Terminal-visual PTY suite (five
  # regressions, several cascading out of fixed-port collisions). Both legs
  # are part of the COMMON PR suite: they run on every CI invocation (the
  # Machine SM dispatches ci.yml per PR head), unconditioned by path — a
  # diff that breaks them must red-block THE PR, never the 3:30 nightly.
  # Main remains backstopped by nightly.yml.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PTY runner picker: prefer the self-hosted fa-m5 minis (dedicated hardware,
  # warm caches, no VM boot, no port contention — the hosted pty-integration
  # leg loses 20-40 min to queue+load flake), fall back to the hosted labels
  # when the pool is busy. GitHub has no OR in runs-on (an array is AND), so
  # the choice happens HERE by counting in-progress jobs already parked on
  # fa-m5 runners (jobs API, actions:read — no admin token needed).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  runner-pick:
    name: Pick PTY runners (fa-m5 or hosted fallback)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      actions: read
    outputs:
      pty_integration: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_integration }}
      pty_visual: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_visual }}
    steps:
      - name: Probe fa-m5 pool and pick
        id: pick
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          M5_POOL: '3'
        run: |
          busy=0
          for rid in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?status=in_progress&per_page=100" --jq '.workflow_runs[].id'); do
            n=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$rid/jobs" --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" and ((.runner_name // "") | startswith("fa-m5")))] | length' || echo 0)
            busy=$((busy + n))
          done
          free=$((M5_POOL - busy))
          if [ "$free" -ge 1 ]; then
            echo "pool: $free free of $M5_POOL fa-m5 -> self-hosted"
            echo 'pty_integration=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "pool: $free free of $M5_POOL fa-m5 -> hosted fallback"
            echo 'pty_integration=["ubuntu-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["macos-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration + cli coverage (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      # SAME secret shape as nightly.yml's pty-integration leg and the
      # Trust model (review 2026-09-23): this is the first pull_request-time
      # leg in ci.yml that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds
      # secrets from forks, so external contributions never see them — but
      # every SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # SAME secret shape as nightly.yml's pty-integration leg and the
      # coverage-gardener that bumps the baseline: the live-provider legs
      # (unlocked by these keys) load extra lib/src/cli surface into the
      # measurement, so a no-key run measures a DIFFERENT — higher —
      # number and would pass while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      # coverage-gardener that bumps the baseline: the live-provider legs
      # (unlocked by these keys) load extra lib/src/cli surface into the
      # measurement, so a no-key run measures a DIFFERENT — higher —
      # number and would pass while the nightly fails. Missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully; the gate stays honest either way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      # Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would
      # try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die. Redirect it to a stable
      # per-runner path (warm across runs); hosted runners are untouched.
      - name: Self-hosted toolcache redirect (fa-m5)
        if: startsWith(runner.name, 'fa-m5')
        run: echo "RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE=${{ runner.workspace }}/toolcache" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: dart test --tags integration (excluding browser-ext)
        run: >-
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
          --coverage=coverage
      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: CLI coverage ratchet (lib/src/cli/**, baseline only up)
        run: python3 scripts/check_cli_coverage.py

  pty-visual:
    name: Terminal visual (PTY screenshots, PR)
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_visual) }}
    needs: [changes, runner-pick]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: touch .env
      - run: cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart
      - run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get
      # The harness spawns `dart bin/fah.dart` FROM THE REPO ROOT; without
      # a root package config it resolves the package to the pub-cache copy
      # (an old published build) and the CLI dies before the first frame.
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/cli_visual --tags integration
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: cli-visual-screenshots-pr
          path: test/integration/screenshots/
          retention-days: 7

  coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 5

blocks.text:
Now I have a clear picture. Key observations comparing nightly.yml's new runner-pick against the existing reference implementation in ci.yml (#860):

**Differences between nightly.yml (this PR) and ci.yml (reference):**

1. **Threshold `free >= 2` vs `free >= 1`**:
   - nightly.yml (this PR): `if [ "$free" -ge 2 ]` → BOTH legs go self-hosted (needs 2 runners simultaneously).
   - ci.yml (reference): `if [ "$free" -ge 1 ]` → both legs go self-hosted if at least 1 free.
   
   Wait, this is interesting — this PR uses `-ge 2` and the reference uses `-ge 1`. Which is right? In nightly, BOTH pty-integration and cli-visual would run concurrently on self-hosted (2 runners needed concurrently, since runner-pick is the only needs, both legs start in parallel). Actually — do they run concurrently? pty-integration and cli-visual both depend only on runner-pick, so yes, they start in parallel. So needing 2 free is arguably MORE correct in nightly than ci.yml's `>= 1`. In ci.yml, with `>= 1`, if only 1 mini is free, one leg grabs it and the other queues on self-hosted... hmm, both jobs request `["self-hosted","macos-m5"]`, so with 1 free runner, one leg starts and the other waits queued (indefinitely?) until a mini frees. GitHub queues self-hosted jobs; they wait until a matching runner is available or the job... queued self-hosted jobs wait forever unless a runner comes online. Actually there's no queue timeout for self-hosted runners by default (jobs can be queued indefinitely? There is a default of 24h? For hosted runners, jobs queued > 24h? Hmm).

   Actually wait — which direction should the reviewer flag? The nightly threshold is arguably better. But there's an inconsistency between the two implementations of the same logic — drift risk. And a subtle behavioral difference: with `-ge 2`, if only 1 mini is free, the nightly falls back to hosted for BOTH legs — but then the 1 free mini sits idle while the hosted legs hit the load flake the PR is trying to avoid. With concurrent jobs = 2, requiring 2 free is the correct conservative approach... but actually it wastes capacity: pty_integration on hosted (flaky) while a mini is idle. Hmm, an alternative would be picking per-leg. Not a blocker; worth a suggestion. Actually wait — is it even true both run simultaneously? runner-pick runs first (3 min max), then both legs start together. So yes, they run concurrently. With pool of 3 and `>= 2`, at least one mini always remains free for... hmm, for what? For ci.yml PR legs (which use `>= 1`)! That's likely deliberate: nightly reserves headroom so PR-time ci.yml legs can still grab a mini. Or so that a concurrent ci.yml run can still get one. Plausibly deliberate. I'll note as a question/suggestion about the divergence from ci.yml's `>= 1` and potential double-booking race.

2. **Race / oversubscription**: counting only `in_progress` jobs, not `queued`. Two nightly-ish runs starting close together (nightly schedule + a manual dispatch, or ci.yml run + nightly run) both probe at roughly the same time before either has jobs in_progress on fa-m5 → both pick self-hosted → legs queue on the minis. Since ci.yml PR legs ALSO run this same probe concurrently (every PR), this race is real: PR-time ci.yml runs and the nightly run will both see free pool and both send jobs to fa-m5. The queued legs then wait on minis with no timeout — nightly.yml's pty-integration and cli-visual have **no timeout-minutes** (I checked the new file: pty-integration has no timeout-minutes; cli-visual has none either), unlike ci.yml's legs (60/45). A queued-on-self-hosted job with no timeout can block the nightly for hours; worse, the auto-issue job has `needs: [full-quality, pty-integration, cli-visual, ...]` with `if: always() && schedule && !cancelled()` — fine, it still files.

   Actually hold on: does GitHub queue self-hosted jobs forever? Jobs queued waiting for a runner will wait until a runner picks them up; there's no default timeout for being queued (the 6-hour job limit applies once running). Hmm, actually if a runner never comes, the job stays queued indefinitely and the run hangs. So the race can genuinely hang the nightly. The mitigating factor: pool busy count includes ci.yml PR legs on fa-m5, so the probe will usually see them. But the probe runs once at runner-pick time; jobs queued after the probe but not yet in_progress are invisible. Flag as IMPORTANT.

3. **N+1 API calls**: The probe loops over up to 100 in-progress runs and makes one `gh api .../runs/$rid/jobs` call per run. In a busy repo (machine-driven PRs — this repo has ai-teammate, machine-merge, etc., so many concurrent runs), that could be dozens of calls; at ~200-500ms each that's 10-30s, OK within timeout-minutes: 3, but with retries/rate limits it could exceed. `gh` auto-retries on 403 rate-limit with backoff (GH_* envs). A cleaner approach: single call to `repos/$REPO/actions/runners` (needs `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runners` — that requires... listing self-hosted runners for a repo requires admin:write? Hmm, actually `gh api repos/REPO/actions/runners` — requires `admin:write`? Docs: "List self-hosted runners for a repository" — fine-grained: "Administration" repository permissions (write). GitHub Apps: administration. So indeed not accessible with actions:read — the comment in the workflow explains this ("jobs API, actions:read — no admin token needed"), which justifies the N+1 workaround. The alternative: use the jobs API pagination smarter, or use `gh api /repos/$REPO/actions/runs?status=in_progress` + `--jq` per run is N+1. Alternative single call: `gh run list --json databaseId --limit 100 --status in_progress` then still N+1. Hmm — there's also the check-runs for a ref... Not simpler. So the N+1 is a known tradeoff already established in ci.yml — consistent with reference. I'll mention only briefly (SUGGESTION): `total_count` guard for >100 runs (pagination ignored → undercount → oversubscription).

4. **`per_page=100` no pagination**: in-progress runs beyond the first 100 aren't counted. Machine-generated repos can have >100 in-progress runs. Undercount → self-hosted chosen when pool is actually busy → queueing. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It's shared with the reference ci.yml implementation. I'd rate SUGGESTION (consistent with existing accepted pattern) or fold into the probe-robustness comment.

5. **cli-visual on fa-m5 without the toolcache redirect**: In nightly.yml's cli-visual job, there is NO "Self-hosted toolcache redirect" step, and it routes to `["self-hosted","macos-m5"]` when free. In ci.yml's pty-visual job — let me check... In the reference (ci.yml pty-visual), there's also no redirect step; but ci.yml's pty-visual doesn't run setup-dart... wait it runs flutter-action. Hmm, the redirect in ci.yml was added only to pty-integration ("Self-hosted fa-m5 minis have no /Users/runner home — setup-* would try to mkdir the hosted toolcache and die"). flutter-action (subosito) doesn't use RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE; it downloads to its own cache dir (~/flutter or RUNNER_TEMP?). # Nightly full-matrix quality run (issue #177, Wave 3 / AC6): the PR-level
# ci.yml was slimmed down for speed, so this workflow preserves the original
# monolith semantics — every gate, full thresholds — on a nightly schedule.
# When a scheduled run goes red, the auto-issue job files (or updates) a
# single deduped `nightly-red` issue.
name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — the nightly-red filing job grants
# issues: write (+ actions: read) in its own job-level block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  full-quality:
    name: Full quality gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - run: dart pub get

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings

      # The example Flutter app lives in this repo; without its package
      # config the repo-wide `dart analyze` cannot resolve Flutter imports.
      - name: Example app pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter pub get

      # The repo-wide `dart analyze` also walks office_addin/dart; without
      # its package config the analyzer cannot resolve
      # `package:fa_office_agent/...` imports (nightly full-quality was red
      # on email_quarantine_test.dart since the add-in landed). ci.yml's
      # analyze job already does this — nightly must match.
      - name: Office add-in pub get (for repo-wide analyze)
        run: dart pub get --directory=office_addin/dart

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # without it the analyzer fails with asset_does_not_exist (a fresh
      # clone hits the same warning locally).
      - name: Create placeholder .env for the example app
        run: touch [REDACTED:Credential File]

      # firebase_options.dart is gitignored (real keys stay local); the
      # repo-wide analyze fails on the unresolved import without it. The
      # tracked placeholder makes it compile (Firebase init is skipped for
      # YOUR_* values at runtime).
      - name: Create placeholder firebase_options.dart for the example app
        run: >-
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart
          flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      - name: dart analyze
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart test --coverage (excluding integration)
        run: dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration

      - name: Format coverage to lcov
        run: dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info

      - name: Coverage ratchet (lib/ >= 80%)
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        run: |
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.9.5"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Duplication guard (lib/ < 1%)
        run: |
          npx --yes jscpd@5 --min-tokens 50 --min-lines 5 --reporters json \
            --output /tmp/jscpd-ci lib/ || true
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import json, sys
          try:
              with open('/tmp/jscpd-ci/jscpd-report.json') as f:
                  pct = json.load(f)['statistics']['total']['percentage']
          except Exception:
              pct = 0.0
          print(f'Duplication: {pct}% (threshold < 1.0%)')
          sys.exit(0 if float(pct) < 1.0 else 1)
          EOF

  # PTY/terminal integration suites (issue #177 follow-up): mock-endpoint
  # tests need NO secrets and always run; live-provider tests self-skip
  # gracefully without keys (their own `skip:` guards), so the blanket
  # "no keys → skip everything" from the old CI job is gone. Coverage over
  # lib/src/cli/** feeds the only-up ratchet (coverage-gardener.yml bumps
  # the baseline weekly) — terminal-test coverage can never silently drop.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PTY runner picker: prefer the self-hosted fa-m5 minis (dedicated hardware,
  # warm caches, no VM boot, no port contention — the hosted pty-integration
  # leg loses 20-40 min to queue+load flake), fall back to the hosted labels
  # when the pool is busy. GitHub has no OR in runs-on (an array is AND), so
  # the choice happens HERE by counting in-progress jobs already parked on
  # fa-m5 runners (jobs API, actions:read — no admin token needed).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  runner-pick:
    name: Pick PTY runners (fa-m5 or hosted fallback)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      actions: read
    outputs:
      pty_integration: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_integration }}
      pty_visual: ${{ steps.pick.outputs.pty_visual }}
    steps:
      - name: Probe fa-m5 pool and pick
        id: pick
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          M5_POOL: '3'
        run: |
          busy=0
          for rid in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs?status=in_progress&per_page=100" --jq '.workflow_runs[].id'); do
            n=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$rid/jobs" --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" and ((.runner_name // "") | startswith("fa-m5")))] | length' || echo 0)
            busy=$((busy + n))
          done
          free=$((M5_POOL - busy))
          if [ "$free" -ge 2 ]; then
            echo "pool: $free free of $M5_POOL fa-m5 -> self-hosted"
            echo 'pty_integration=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["self-hosted","macos-m5"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "pool: $free free of $M5_POOL fa-m5 -> hosted fallback"
            echo 'pty_integration=["ubuntu-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo 'pty_visual=["macos-latest"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  pty-integration:
    name: PTY/CLI integration + cli coverage
    runs-on: ${{ fromJSON(needs.runner-pick.outputs.pty_integration) }}
    needs: runner-pick
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

- name: dart test under hostile ambient env

  # red on main night after night before anyone looked — the CLI-coverage

   - ci.yml (reference): `if [ "$free" -ge 1 ]` → both legs go self-hosted if at least 1 free.

Actually — do they run concurrently? pty-integration and cli-visual both depend only on runner-pick, so yes, they start in parallel. So needing 2 free is arguably MORE correct in nightly than ci.yml's `>= 1`. In ci.yml, with `>= 1`, if only 1 mini is free, one leg grabs it and the other queues on self-hosted... hmm, both jobs request `["self-hosted","macos-m5"]`, so with 1 free runner, one leg starts and the other waits queued (indefinitely?) until a mini frees. GitHub queues self-hosted jobs; they wait until a matching runner is available or the job... queued self-hosted jobs wait forever unless a runner comes online. Actually wait — is it even true both run simultaneously? runner-pick runs first (3 min max), then both legs start together. So yes, they run concurrently. Two nightly-ish runs starting close together (nightly schedule + a manual dispatch, or ci.yml run + nightly run) both probe at roughly the same time before either has jobs in_progress on fa-m5 → both pick self-hosted → legs queue on the minis. Jobs queued waiting for a runner will wait until a runner picks them up; there's no default timeout for being queued (the 6-hour job limit applies once running). The mitigating factor: pool busy count includes ci.yml PR legs on fa-m5, so the probe will usually see them. But the probe runs once at runner-pick time; jobs queued after the probe but not yet in_progress are invisible. Flag as IMPORTANT.

In a busy repo (machine-driven PRs — this repo has ai-teammate, machine-merge, etc., so many concurrent runs), that could be dozens of calls; at ~200-500ms each that's 10-30s, OK within timeout-minutes: 3, but with retries/rate limits it could exceed. `gh` auto-retries on 403 rate-limit with backoff (GH_* envs). Let me not over-assert. The important comparability point: ci.yml's pty-visual leg runs the same flutter-action on fa-m5 with NO redirect, and presumably it worked (it's merged and running — the nightly comment says ci.yml legs already run this).
